correctness.rationale: The diagonal lengths are 2 and 2t and the area is 2t. In the two angular quadrants the projection extrema give W=W0+D with W0=cos(theta)+t sin(theta)+|cos(theta)-t sin(theta)| and D=(|s cos(theta) minus-or-plus h sin(theta)|-|cos(theta)-t sin(theta)|)_+. For fixed t the entire change is within O_t(epsilon) of theta0=arctan(1/t). On that interval the model d=(|a+b xi|-R|xi|)_+ has a=(ts minus-or-plus h)/R and b=O_t(epsilon); the uniform pointwise model error is O_t(epsilon^3) on the union of the supports, and hence gives O_t(epsilon^4) integral error even at a switching line. The two triangles have widths |a|/(R minus-or-plus sign(a)b), giving total area a^2 R/(R^2-b^2)=a^2/R+O_t(epsilon^4) and first signed moment O_t(epsilon^4). Each of the integrals of 2R|xi|d and d^2 is 2|a|^3/(3R)+O_t(epsilon^4), so both are required in the second moment. Base quadrant integrals are 2R and I0. Summing the two quadrants with weight 1/pi and dividing the second moment by the square of the first gives exactly the claimed coefficients. Independently, Cauchy–Schwarz gives I0>=8R^2/pi>=16t/pi>4t, so the quadratic form is strictly negative at every fixed t; the cubic and uniform remainder cannot change the nearby sign. Along a single axis the nonzero |h|^3 term also forbids a cubic Taylor polynomial. These are local at fixed t; arbitrary quadrilaterals are implicated only in ruling out local minimization. The stored Simpson checker reports 203 finite regressions; a separate piecewise exact-in-angle integration script /workspace/branches/5a46a59c-66b6-45b4-b133-05159763f20a/independent_width_check.py cross-checked the edge-kernel moments and 36 mixed paths at t=0.7,1,1.8, including both switching lines. The largest sampled scaled fourth-order residual was about 0.00338806. These tests are not the uniform proof.
